outlook: Wheat led grains lower Wednesday after Russia signaled it would join trilateral Black Sea talks, raising the prospect of fuller Russian and Ukrainian exports; December Chicago wheat closed down 15 cents at $6.28¼ and Minneapolis December spring wheat fell 11¼ cents to $6.50½. Corn slipped 1¼ cents to $4.60¾ with the U.S. harvest past the halfway mark and Brazil crop estimates rising. November soybeans lost 6½ cents to $12.41¾ even with flash sales to China and Spain announced. ICE November canola dropped C$8 to C$773 as vegetable oils traded weaker.
